lessons.title: Structured vs Unstructured Data
lessons.content_md:
# Two Types of Clues 📂

As a data detective, the clues you find will come in two completely different forms: **Structured Data** and **Unstructured Data**.

## The Filing Cabinet (Structured Data)

Imagine a perfectly organized filing cabinet. Every folder has a name, every paper has a date, and everything is neatly categorized in alphabetical order. 

This is **Structured Data**. 

It is data that fits perfectly into rows and columns, like an Excel spreadsheet or a standard database. It is incredibly easy for a computer to read, search, and analyze.

Examples include:
- Bank account balances
- Excel spreadsheets of customer names
- Store inventory logs

<flipcard front="🗄️ What is Structured Data?" back="Highly organized data that fits perfectly into rows and columns, making it very easy to search and analyze."></flipcard>

## The Messy Box of Photos (Unstructured Data)

Now imagine going to the attic and finding a giant, dusty cardboard box dumped full of thousands of random photographs, old cassette tapes, and crumpled letters. There are no folders. There is no order.

This is **Unstructured Data**.

It is data that does not fit into a neat spreadsheet. It's messy, complicated, and requires advanced AI to make sense of.

Examples include:
- Millions of tweets and Facebook posts
- Audio recordings of customer service calls
- Traffic camera footage

<flipcard front="📦 What is Unstructured Data?" back="Messy, complex data like text, images, and audio that cannot easily fit into a spreadsheet or traditional database."></flipcard>

<flipcard front="⚖️ Which type of data is more common?" back="Unstructured Data! Over 80% of all data generated in the world today is unstructured (videos, social media posts, emails, etc)."></flipcard>
